task_name: Cedar Commons - Farmers market identity restoration
client_brief:
Recover the market's apron mark and prepare our site photographs

Hello from Cedar Commons. We help run the farmers' market, and the apron print is the version of our mark people recognise. Could you help us get it into a form we can place cleanly, without a box around it?

Final handoff

brand_identity.sector: A volunteer-run weekend farmers market in a municipal park, free to the public, funded by daily stall fees.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2016, in a park in Burlington, Vermont. Volunteer-run, 36 to 44 stalls, open weekends May through October.
brand_identity.about: Cedar Commons is a neighbourhood farmers market that runs on weekends in a Burlington park, free to walk into and funded entirely by the vendors who pay a daily stall fee. It has outgrown its chalkboards and its bedsheet banner. The signage exists to get families to the right lot, past the entrance and to the stall they are looking for, printed cheaply and well at a local sign shop.
brand_identity.audience: Neighbourhood families and weekend walkers who arrive on foot or park in the wrong lot, plus the vendors and volunteers who run the morning. Read from a moving car and from across a field.
brand_identity.price_positioning: A free public market funded by 25 to 60 dollar daily stall fees, often part-donated. Everything prints on coroplast and vinyl at a local sign shop. Flat inks and heavy type, never a refined tint palette that would be unreadable outdoors and would make a free market look like it is charging.
brand_identity.typography: Display in a friendly high-contrast slab or bold grotesque, weighted to be read from a car. Wayfinding and schedule copy in a plain heavy sans with one clear instruction per sign. Real weight matters more than refinement.
brand_identity.voice: Warm, plain and welcoming, like a volunteer at the gate. Example line: "Cheerful, legible from a distance, few colours, and it lives outdoors in the rain. Not precious. Tell us what our mark can and cannot do."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The market mark was drawn nine years ago by a volunteer's cousin, who is not reachable, and screen-printed onto aprons and tote bags. No file of any kind was ever kept. The best surviving copy is a photograph of one apron folded on a picnic table. There is no vector art, so the mark has to be recovered from that photograph rather than redrawn.
brand_identity.values: Community and thrift. Recover the real mark rather than replace it, keep the set to a few flat inks that print cheaply, and tell the committee what the mark can and cannot do before they pay for plates.
